lines.text: Americans' view of the economy right now hit a record low.
lines.say: Americans' view of the economy right now hit a record low.

lines.text: The University of Michigan's current conditions gauge fell to 44.7 in early October, from 50.9 in September.
lines.say: The University of Michigan's current conditions gauge fell to forty-four point seven in early October, down from fifty point nine in September.

lines.text: Its overall sentiment index slipped to 46.3, the lowest since May's record low of 44.8.
lines.say: Its overall sentiment index slipped to forty-six point three, the lowest since May's record low of forty-four point eight.

lines.text: Survey director Joanne Hsu said views on buying big-ticket items plunged, citing high prices and borrowing costs.
lines.say: Survey director Joanne Hsu said views on buying big-ticket items plunged, citing high prices and borrowing costs.

lines.text: She said lower-income people and those with smaller stock portfolios took the steepest hit.

lines.text: People now expect 4.7% inflation over the next year, up from 4.6% in September.
lines.say: People now expect four point seven percent inflation over the next year, up from four point six in September.

lines.text: Remember, this measures mood, not spending. Gloomy surveys don't always mean people stop buying.
lines.say: Remember, this measures mood, not spending, and gloomy surveys don't always mean people stop buying.

lines.text: The final October reading comes out October 23.

post.title: Americans' View of the Economy Right Now Hits a Record Low
post.ig:
Americans' view of the economy right now hit a record low.
The University of Michigan's current conditions index fell to 44.7 in its early October 2026 reading, from 50.9 in September, the lowest on record.
The overall sentiment index slipped to 46.3 from 48.1, the lowest since May's record low of 44.8.
Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7% from 4.6%. Survey director Joanne Hsu said lower-income people and those with smaller stock portfolios saw the steepest drops.
Sources: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, CNN, Bloomberg, Benzinga.
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc:
The University of Michigan's current economic conditions index fell to a record low of 44.7 in its preliminary October 2026 survey, released Oct 9, down from 50.9 in September. The overall sentiment index slipped to 46.3, the lowest since May's record low of 44.8, and year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7%. Sources: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, CNN, Bloomberg. News and education, not financial advice.
